cf.title: Introduce XID age based replication slot invalidation

input.subject: Introduce XID age based replication slot invalidation

verdict_reasoning: The goal is accepted in the thread and no objection at level 1a or 1b survived. Level 2 fails on four reproduced or unanswered design problems: replication-ondisk-1, replication-ondisk-4, replication-ondisk-2 and replication-ondisk-3. Their fixes exist only as descriptions in messages #62 to #64, not in a posted patch. maintenance-fit-1 adds that each slot owner needed its own handling and the design gives no general rule.

brief.title: Invalidate replication slots by xmin age with max_slot_xid_age
brief.problem: An idle, forgotten or lagging replication slot holds xmin or catalog_xmin back, so vacuum cannot freeze and the cluster moves toward XID wraparound. max_slot_wal_keep_size covers WAL, and idle_replication_slot_timeout is hard to set across a fleet with different XID rates. The target is operators of many clusters who want write availability over keeping slots.
brief.proposed_design: A new GUC max_slot_xid_age invalidates a slot when its effective xmin or catalog_xmin is older than the limit. The checkpointer and restartpoint check all slots, and vacuum checks per relation in heap_vacuum_rel, but only unheld slots and only when a slot holds OldestXmin. v15 has three patches: the checkpoint path, the vacuum path, and invalidation of synced slots on standbys.
user_visible_surface: GUC max_slot_xid_age (integer, 0 disables, max equal to vacuum_failsafe_age, postgresql.conf or command line only).
New invalidation_reason value xid_aged in pg_replication_slots.
New log messages for xid_aged invalidation, with the slot's xmin or catalog_xmin age.
pg_createsubscriber disables XID-age invalidation during its run, like the idle timeout.
Proposed changes to how the pg_conflict_detection slot and hot_standby_feedback catalog_xmin respond to the limit.
author_claims: Invalidating a slot whose xmin is older than the limit lets vacuum freeze and avoids wraparound without manual vacuum or downtime.
Setting the GUC at or just below vacuum_failsafe_age (1.6 billion) is the intended use.
The per-relation check costs little because it reuses OldestXmin and slot horizons from one ComputeXidHorizons call.
Vacuum never waits on a held slot, and the checkpointer invalidates held slots on its regular pass.
Invalidated slots behave like those of other invalidation causes; the feature is off by default.
brief.thread_state: Sawada, Bertrand, Amit, Nisha, Kuroda and others reviewed the patch in depth, and v15 needs a rebase. Open items are the pg_conflict_detection slot, standby physical slots invalidated through hot_standby_feedback, and slots invalidated while a long transaction holds the horizon.
unclear: Kuroda cited Robert Haas's earlier objection that a cutoff age is hard to choose; the thread does not show him agreeing.
Held slots can wait up to checkpoint_timeout before invalidation; the thread gives no estimate of what that delay means near wraparound.
Synced slots invalidated on a standby are dropped, recreated as temporary and never sync again while the primary slot stays old; the fix is not settled.
No performance numbers are given for many slots or many tables.
The proposed launcher flag for retain_dead_tuples subscriptions may not survive a restart, per Bertrand.

objections.title: Primary invalidates a healthy standby's physical slot through forwarded catalog_xmin
objections.failure_scenario: An operator sets max_slot_xid_age on the primary, and a failover subscription is disabled. hot_standby_feedback copies the synced slot's old catalog_xmin onto the standby's physical slot, and the next checkpoint invalidates that slot. The standby then loops on "can no longer access replication slot" and may need a rebuild once WAL is gone.
objections.argument: Message #60 reproduced this on v15, with the physical slot invalidated while its xmin age was 0. With the slot in synchronized_standby_slots, other failover slots also stall. The fix proposed in message #63 changes what hot_standby_feedback means: the primary would clamp the received catalog_xmin, and standby slots would fail later as rows_removed. That fix is not yet in a posted patch, and it changes behaviour that users of hot_standby_feedback depend on today.
objections.author_must_show: With the feedback clamp in place, what does a standby operator see and log, and how do they tell the primary's max_slot_xid_age was the cause?

critic.reasoning: Message #60 reproduced the physical slot invalidation on v15, and the clamp agreed in message #63 is not in a posted patch. Message #60 itself notes the misleading rows_removed reason on the standby, and no message resolves it.

objections.title: Healthy logical slots invalidated when a transaction holds the horizon
objections.failure_scenario: A long open transaction, or a repeatable read snapshot without an XID, pins catalog_xmin on the publisher. The checkpoint invalidates every caught-up logical slot, and their subscriptions break. Vacuum gains nothing, because the transaction still holds the same cutoff.
objections.argument: Message #61 shows this on v15 with an active, caught-up slot. Message #62 proposes a new proc-array scan in the checkpointer, with a database OID and KnownAssignedXids handling on standbys. That scan exists only as a description. Until it lands, the checkpoint path can break replication for a cause that slot invalidation cannot fix.
objections.author_must_show: How does the checkpoint path prove a slot is the actual horizon holder, on primary and standby, before it invalidates the slot?

critic.reasoning: Message #61 reproduced the invalidation of an active, caught-up slot with no vacuum gain, and the check proposed in message #62 is not in a patch. The snapshot-only case in #62 shows no vacuum gain, but it does not show pinned caught-up slots.

objections.title: Launcher retention flag for pg_conflict_detection is not crash-safe
objections.failure_scenario: The launcher stops counting a disabled subscription and lets the slot's xmin advance, but subretentionactive stays true in pg_subscription. The server restarts with the new xmin already persisted. When the subscription is enabled, its apply worker believes retention was continuous and runs conflict detection over tuples that vacuum has already removed.
objections.argument: Message #64 keeps the stop decision in launcher shared memory because the launcher cannot update pg_subscription. Message #65 asks what happens across a postmaster restart, and the thread has no answer yet. The design also stops retention for all subscriptions, while message #57 and message #58 agreed to stop only the subscriptions holding the xmin. The persisted slot xmin and the catalog flag can disagree, and no step in the design brings them back in line.
objections.author_must_show: What makes the slot's persisted xmin and subretentionactive agree after a crash between the launcher's decision and the apply worker's catalog update?

critic.reasoning: Message #65 asks what happens when the cleared slot xmin is persisted and the postmaster restarts while subretentionactive is still true. The thread ends there without an answer, so the design for pg_conflict_detection is open.

objections.title: Synced slots churn and are lost at promotion
objections.failure_scenario: sync_replication_slots is on, and the primary's failover slot is idle. The standby's restartpoint invalidates the synced slot, and slotsync recreates it as temporary with a newer catalog_xmin, so it never syncs again. The checkpointer then SIGTERMs the slot sync worker about every max_slot_xid_age XIDs, and the slot is gone after promotion.
objections.argument: Message #53 reproduced this on v14, including the xid_aged reason disappearing so nothing remains to alert on. Message #54 and message #55 accept it as matching max_slot_wal_keep_size, and v15 only updates a comment (message #59). This feature targets slots whose horizon does not advance, so the stuck case is its normal case. For max_slot_wal_keep_size the same case is a rare corner.
objections.author_must_show: After a synced slot is invalidated for XID age, how does the operator learn a failover slot is missing before promotion, and how is the periodic worker termination stopped?

critic.reasoning: Message #54 argues that max_slot_wal_keep_size has the same behaviour, but that case was not reproduced. This feature targets slots whose horizon does not advance, so the stuck slot and the repeated slot sync worker termination from message #53 are its expected case.

objections.title: Each slot-owning subsystem needs its own xid_aged handling
objections.failure_scenario: A later release adds a new internal slot owner, such as another launcher-managed or temporary decoding slot. Nobody adds an xid_aged exception or back-off path for it, so it is treated as an ordinary slot. Months later an operator with max_slot_xid_age set finds that feature broken or looping after a checkpoint, with only an invalidation LOG line.
objections.argument: Most open work in the thread is per-consumer special cases, not the core check. Message #53 reports a churn loop for synced slots. Message #57 and message #64 give pg_conflict_detection a launcher shmem flag protocol, and message #63 adds a feedback clamp for hot_standby_feedback. The design gives later slot owners no rule to follow and no check that fails when they ignore one, so the rule has to be relearned per feature (message #59 tested repack slots by hand).
objections.author_must_show: What general rule tells a future slot owner how to react to xid_aged, and what would fail in tests if a new slot type did not follow it?

critic.reasoning: The thread shows three slot owners that each needed their own handling: synced slots, pg_conflict_detection and physical slots fed by hot_standby_feedback. Review found each one, and the proposal states no general rule or test that would catch the next one.

refuted.title: Earlier objection on choosing the cutoff age is not yet answered
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator sets max_slot_xid_age well below vacuum_failsafe_age to limit bloat on a cluster with a high XID rate. A healthy subscriber that lags during a nightly batch passes the limit, and its slot is invalidated. The subscription stops and needs a full resync, which the operator finds out about the next morning.
refuted.argument: Message #19 reports that an earlier XID-based proposal met the objection that a cutoff age is hard to choose, and that the code may not be accepted without that objector's agreement. Message #20 links a summary and recommends setting the GUC near 1.6 billion, but the GUC accepts any value from 1 up to that limit. Messages #61 and #62 show the age signal can still invalidate healthy slots when a long transaction holds the horizon. The thread does not show the original objector agreeing.
refuted.author_must_show: Why accept any value below vacuum_failsafe_age, instead of a much narrower range, if the only supported use is avoiding wraparound near the failsafe threshold?

critic.reasoning: Message #20 answers the cutoff question with a concrete value tied to vacuum_failsafe_age, and message #24 caps the GUC there. The low-value scenario costs only an operator who ignores that guidance, and the long-transaction part duplicates replication-ondisk-4.

refuted.title: Primary-side GUC quietly changes what hot_standby_feedback guarantees
refuted.failure_scenario: A primary admin sets max_slot_xid_age. The primary then caps or ignores the catalog_xmin a standby reports, and vacuum removes catalog rows the standby still needs. The standby admin sees logical slots invalidated as rows_removed and looks for the cause on the standby, but the cause was a setting on the primary.
refuted.argument: Message #60 shows that v15 invalidates the standby's physical slot and breaks streaming. The fix agreed in message #63 has the primary store a catalog_xmin newer than the one the standby sent, and log it. Today hot_standby_feedback is a promise that the reported horizon is honoured. With the fix it becomes conditional on a primary GUC, and invalidation_reason on the standby names the wrong cause. Message #60 already notes this downside, but no design has settled it.
refuted.author_must_show: How will a standby operator tell from pg_replication_slots or the logs that a rows_removed invalidation came from the primary's max_slot_xid_age?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which covers the same feedback clamp and the same misleading rows_removed reason on the standby.

refuted.title: Server GUC overrides per-subscription retain_dead_tuples without durable state
refuted.failure_scenario: A user enables retain_dead_tuples on a disabled subscription. The launcher stops honouring its retention because of max_slot_xid_age, but pg_subscription still shows subretentionactive true. After a restart, the subscription can believe it retains dead tuples that vacuum has already removed, so conflicts go undetected.
refuted.argument: The pg_conflict_detection design changed several times in messages #49 to #64, and it is still open. In the latest proposal (message #64), the launcher keeps a stop flag in shared memory because it cannot update pg_subscription. Message #65 asks what happens if the cleared slot xmin is persisted before a restart, and the thread has no answer. Message #65 also notes that the proposal stops healthy subscriptions too, so one slot-age GUC now changes a user-visible subscription option for more subscriptions than it needs to.
refuted.author_must_show: After a crash between the launcher's stop decision and the apply worker's catalog update, what do pg_subscription and the slot show, and do they agree?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2, which states the same restart gap between the launcher's shared-memory flag and subretentionactive more directly.

refuted.title: Any session holding an old snapshot can get healthy slots invalidated
refuted.failure_scenario: A role with only CONNECT and SELECT opens a REPEATABLE READ transaction and leaves it idle. After max_slot_xid_age transactions, the next checkpoint invalidates every caught-up logical slot pinned behind it and terminates their walsenders. Vacuum gains nothing, and the operator finds broken subscriptions that need a full resync after the session ends.
refuted.argument: Message #61 shows a long transaction pinning catalog_xmin of active logical slots, and the checkpoint invalidating them with no vacuum gain. Message #62 adds that a snapshot-only backend with no XID has the same effect, and proposes a new proc-array check that v15 does not contain and nobody has reviewed. Without the feature, cancelling that session recovers everything. With it, a session that needs no special privilege can cause permanent loss of replication state.
refuted.author_must_show: How does the next version ensure that a slot is invalidated only when the slot itself, and not a user backend, holds the vacuum horizon, on both the checkpoint and vacuum paths?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-4, with the same failure and the same required fix. Message #61 also ties the pinned catalog_xmin to a transaction that has an XID, so the snapshot-only variant is not shown to pin caught-up slots.

refuted.title: Fix for standby feedback changes hot_standby_feedback semantics on the primary
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator sets max_slot_xid_age on a primary that serves a standby with logical decoding slots. The primary silently clamps the catalog_xmin it receives through hot_standby_feedback. Later the standby's slots are invalidated as rows_removed, and the operator looks for a conflict on the standby instead of the age limit on the primary.
refuted.argument: Message #60 and message #63 move from invalidating the physical slot to having the primary override the catalog_xmin a standby reports. The protection that hot_standby_feedback gives then depends on a setting the standby cannot see, and the reason recorded on the standby is wrong, as message #60 notes. This new mechanism is larger than the original slot check and is not yet in v15. It would become behaviour the project has to keep defending.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the feedback clamp be proposed and reviewed separately, and how would a standby operator learn that the primary's max_slot_xid_age caused their rows_removed invalidations?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which already covers the feedback clamp, its absence from v15 and the wrong cause shown on the standby.

refuted.title: Age-based slot cleanup is already possible with a monitoring query and pg_drop_replication_slot
refuted.failure_scenario: A fleet operator already runs a job that reads age(xmin) and age(catalog_xmin) from pg_replication_slots, calls pg_terminate_backend on the holder and then pg_drop_replication_slot. With the patch, core keeps three invalidation paths plus special cases for the pg_conflict_detection slot and hot_standby_feedback, while that job covers most of the same slots.
refuted.argument: Message #43 shows that slot XID age is one query against pg_replication_slots, and the limit is a fixed XID count, so one threshold works across a fleet with different XID rates. Message #1 rules out idle_replication_slot_timeout only, and the thread never weighs an external age-based job. Core does add synced slots on standbys, which users cannot drop, and an invalidation_reason kept for later inspection. Messages #57 to #65 show the scope growing into the launcher, subscriptions and feedback handling.
refuted.author_must_show: Which slots does an external job that terminates and drops slots by XID age fail to handle, and do those cases alone justify vacuum, checkpointer and launcher changes in core?

critic.reasoning: The objection itself concedes that an external job cannot drop synced slots on standbys. Core already has max_slot_wal_keep_size and idle_replication_slot_timeout for the same class of problem, and reviewers from several companies accepted the motivation in messages #2 and #8.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch invalidates replication slots in the checkpointer, restartpoint and vacuum, and affects synced slots and hot_standby_feedback.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: pg_replication_slots gains invalidation_reason xid_aged, and the pg_conflict_detection design interacts with subretentionactive in pg_subscription.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: src/include/replication/slot.h changes, which adds a new invalidation cause visible to code that uses slots.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: The patch adds max_slot_xid_age, off by default, capped at vacuum_failsafe_age.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-1: Primary invalidates a healthy standby's physical slot through forwarded catalog_xmin

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Synced slots, pg_conflict_detection and hot_standby_feedback each need their own xid_aged handling, and later slot owners will too.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Vacuum checks slots per relation in heap_vacuum_rel; the thread gives no numbers for many slots or many tables.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: With the feedback clamp from message #63, what does a standby operator see in pg_replication_slots and the logs that points to the primary's max_slot_xid_age?
How does the checkpoint path prove, on primary and standby, that a slot and not a backend holds the horizon before it invalidates the slot?
After a restart between the launcher's stop decision and the apply worker's catalog update, what makes the slot's persisted xmin and subretentionactive agree?
After a synced slot is invalidated for XID age, how does the operator learn before promotion that a failover slot is missing?
What general rule tells a future slot owner how to react to xid_aged, and which test fails if a new slot type ignores it?

committability.owner_note: The review notes say Sawada co-wrote much of the design and Amit is engaged. The owner must know slot invalidation, slot sync and the vacuum horizon code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for every case where a slot is invalidated that should not be, across physical, logical, synced and conflict-detection slots, and for the changed hot_standby_feedback behaviour, for as long as the GUC exists.
committability.author_follow_up: The patch reached v15 over more than a year with responses to review, and the CommitFest entry was created in August 2026. v15 needs a rebase.

priority.reason: Operators of slot-heavy fleets gain from it and the thread accepts the motivation. Four reproduced or open design problems have fixes only as descriptions, and they reach into the checkpointer, vacuum, slot sync, the launcher and feedback handling.

provisional_note: Only the prose of the first two patch versions was read, not the v15 code. The cost of the per-relation vacuum check and the exact behaviour of the fixes proposed in messages #62 to #64 could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: Error "initial slot snapshot too large" in create replication slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the "initial slot snapshot too large" error in CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT, which happens because SnapBuildInitialSnapshot puts top-level and subtransaction XIDs into the xip array and the count can exceed GetMaxSnapshotXidCount(). Versions tried excluding subtransactions, marking the snapshot takenDuringRecovery, asking the reorder buffer which XIDs are subtransactions, and finally using the subxip array as an extension of xip.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to the last version because it adds a third way of using the xip and subxip arrays, and he saw no consensus on an approach. Earlier approaches failed for other reasons: the reorder buffer cannot reliably tell subtransactions apart, using takenDuringRecovery was rejected, and resizing xip made procarray.c and snapmgr.c too complicated. The author withdrew the entry for lack of a simple fix.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's bad enough that we
already use the xip/subxip arrays in two different ways depending on
the situation. Increasing that to three different ways seems painful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes StartReplication() reject a physical replication slot that has already been invalidated, for example by max_slot_wal_keep_size, as the logical walsender already does. Without it a walsender can stream from an invalidated slot, move its restart_lsn forward, and pg_replication_slots shows it as valid while it protects neither WAL nor rows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding to review questions, so vignesh C moved the entry to Waiting on Author and then to Returned with Feedback. Ashutosh Bapat asked how a build before commit 15f8203 behaves and warned that changing long-released behaviour of physical slots could break backward compatibility. Robert Haas noted that the documentation does not match the current behaviour and that the intended interaction with physical slots is not clear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think making logical and physical slot behaviour consistent would be
better but if the inconsistent behaviour is out there for some
releases, changing that now will break backward compatibility.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add function pg_advance_replication_slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a SQL function that moves a physical replication slot forward to a given WAL position without consuming the WAL, for example to keep slots in sync across servers. Later versions named it pg_advance_replication_slot, allowed forward moves only, and raised an error on logical slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier asked that moving the slot backwards raise an error with the current slot position instead of a warning, and that the logical-slot error use ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED. Andres Freund added that neither message followed the message style guidelines. The patch got no update in the following two months, so it was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
True as well, and the patch did not get an update in two months to
reflect that. So I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add recovery TAP test for race condition with slot invalidations"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add recovery TAP test for race condition with slot invalidations"
Reverted commit(s): Add recovery TAP test for race condition with slot invalidations
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 08a52ab151ca, due to some sporadic instability in
the test.  Getting the test right should require some redesign with a
second injection point, but let's revert it for now to avoid these
issues in the CI as a lot of patches are under discussion in this last
commit fest.

Per buildfarm members hachi and gokiburi.

precedents_retrieved.title: Upper limit arguments of pg_logical_slot_xxx_changes functions accept invalid values
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_logical_slot_get_changes_guts() set upto_nchanges to 0 instead of InvalidXLogRecPtr when the argument is NULL. It also rejects negative upto_nchanges values and invalid upto_lsn values with an error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier noted that a negative upto_nchanges can reasonably mean unlimited, and the author then offered to fix only the InvalidXLogRecPtr assignment. Robert Haas argued that the current code is no less robust than the proposed form and should stay as it is. Michael Paquier closed the entry because the existing behavior has been in place for several releases.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I am not prepared to spend much time arguing about it, but I think we
should just leave this the way it is.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
Reverted commit(s): Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2aa6e33, that added a fast path to skip
anti-wraparound and non-aggressive autovacuum jobs (these have no sense
as anti-wraparound implies aggressive).  With a cluster using a high
amount of relations with a portion of them being heavily updated, this
could cause autovacuum to lock down, with autovacuum workers attempting
repeatedly those jobs on the same relations for the same database, that
just kept being skipped.  This lock down can be solved with a manual
VACUUM FREEZE.

Justin King has reported one environment where the issue happened, and
Julien Rouhaud and I have been able to reproduce it in a second
environment.  With a very aggressive autovacuum_freeze_max_age,
triggering those jobs with pgbench is a matter of minutes, and hitting
the lock down is a lot harder (my local tests failed to do that).

Note that anti-wraparound and non-aggressive jobs can only be triggered
on a subset of shared catalogs:
- pg_auth_members
- pg_authid
- pg_database
- pg_replication_origin
- pg_shseclabel
- pg_subscription
- pg_tablespace
While the lock down was possible down to v12, the root cause of those
jobs is a much older issue, which needs more analysis.

Bonus thanks to Andres Freund for the discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: Autovacuum: vacuum tables in descending order of xid_age
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Mark Dilger, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes autovacuum sort the tables of a database by descending xid age (relfrozenxid age) and vacuum the oldest first, instead of the current pg_class order. The author proposed this single change first, with other scheduling factors left to later patches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers judged sorting by xid age alone too simple, so it could regress as many cases as it improved. Robert Haas showed that a table that takes longer to vacuum can need to start first even though it is younger, and asked for a formula that also weighs table size, index size and bloat. Mark Dilger and Michael Paquier worried about regressions from changing default autovacuum behavior. The thread then stalled without consensus.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: A lot of previous efforts to improve autovacuum scheduling have fallen down precisely because they did something that was so simple that it was doomed to regress as many cases as it improved, so I wouldn't be too quick to dismiss Mark's suggestion.

precedents_retrieved.title: expose confirmed_flush for replication slots
precedents_retrieved.summary: expose confirmed_flush for replication slots

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
Reverted commit(s): VACUUM: ignore indexing operations with CONCURRENTLY
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit d9d076222f5b "VACUUM: ignore indexing operations
with CONCURRENTLY".

These changes caused indexes created with the CONCURRENTLY option to
miss heap tuples that were HOT-updated and HOT-pruned during the index
creation.  Before these changes, HOT pruning would have been prevented
by the Xmin of the transaction creating the index, but because this
change was precisely to allow the Xmin to move forward ignoring that
backend, now other backends scanning the table can prune them.  This is
not a problem for VACUUM (which requires a lock that conflicts with a
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY operation), but HOT-prune can definitely
occur.  In other words, Xmin advancement was sped up, but at the cost of
corrupting the resulting index.

Regrettably, this means that the new feature in PG14 that RIC/CIC on
very large tables no longer force VACUUM to retain very old tuples goes
away.  We might try to implement it again in a later release, but for
now the risk of indexes missing tuples is too high and there's no easy
fix.

Backpatch to 14, where this change appeared.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_replslotdata - a tool for displaying replication slot information
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Michael Paquier, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new client-side tool, pg_replslotdata, reads the binary replication slot files under pg_replslot/ and prints slot information such as restart LSN, xid, slot type and two-phase state. It works while the server is down, in the same way as pg_controldata and pg_waldump.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Committers judged that the use cases did not justify the cost of maintaining a separate tool in core, including its documentation and translations, and that most needs can be met with an online server. Since the tool is entirely client side, reviewers suggested keeping it in an external repository. The author agreed to drop the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Weighed against the cost of maintaining (including documentation) a separate
tool this doesn't seem sufficient reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix cancelled queries when hot_standby_feedback = on
precedents_retrieved.summary: With hot_standby_feedback = on, standby queries still get cancelled when vacuum truncates a heap on the primary, because the AccessExclusiveLock taken for truncation is replayed on the standby. The final patch adds a new lock level, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE LOCAL, that vacuum uses for heap truncation and that is not WAL-logged, so standby queries must tolerate concurrent truncation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane showed that letting scans run during truncation leaves a race: concurrent scans can load to-be-truncated pages back into shared buffers before ftruncate, and reading past EOF on a standby can extend the relation. Alexander Korotkov agreed the patch had to be revised and sketched a new truncation design, but Robert Haas called it fragile and doubted it prevents stale buffers from being taken as valid. No new version followed, the existing patch failed initdb, and the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we ever have valid-looking buffers in shared_buffers after the corresponding data has been truncated away on disk, we've got to make sure that nobody ever confuses one of them with an actually-valid buffer.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
Reverted commit(s): Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 06f5295 as per issues with this approach, both in
terms of efficiency impact and stability.  First, contrary to the
single-item cache for transaction IDs in transam.c, the cache may finish
by not be hit for a long time, and without an invalidation mechanism to
clear it, it would cause inconsistent results on wraparound for
example.  Second, the use of SubTransGetTopmostTransaction() for the
caching has a limited impact on performance.  SubTransGetParent() could
have more impact, though the benchmarking of the single-item approach
still needs to be proved, particularly under the conditions where SLRU
lookups are stressed in parallel with overflowed snapshots (aka more
than 64 subxids generated, for example).

After discussion with Andres Freund.

roaster_notes.note: [P4] concerns rejecting already invalidated physical slots. Its backward-compatibility reason does not apply to an opt-in GUC that is off by default.

The GUC itself follows the existing pattern of max_slot_wal_keep_size and idle_replication_slot_timeout, adds no syntax, and is off by default. The synced-slot recreation behaviour also matches the existing WAL case (messages #54 to #56).
No on-disk format, WAL record, or catalog column change is described beyond a new invalidation_reason value, so pg_upgrade is not affected.
Only superusers or the server config can set the GUC. The new view value and log lines expose slot xmin ages that pg_replication_slots already shows. I found no other privilege exposure.

Hot-path cost and ownership were checked and give no objection. The vacuum check reuses horizons from one ComputeXidHorizons call and runs only when a slot holds OldestXmin. Sawada, a committer who knows the area, co-wrote much of the design, and Amit is engaged.
Only one objection from this angle. The feature extends the existing slot invalidation mechanism and does not duplicate it.

The material shows enough demand. Slots that hold xmin or catalog_xmin toward wraparound are a known failure, and reviewers from several companies (messages #2, #8, #16, #38) accept the motivation. Costs fall mainly on users who set the GUC, since it is off by default. A monitoring query plus a script that drops slots is a workaround, but it needs every operator to build the same safety net against wraparound, so I do not raise 'not now, show demand'.
